question.prompt: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values (i.e., from left to right, level by level).
expectedPoints: Record queue size at start of each level to process batch
Add left and right child nodes to queue
O(N) time and O(N) space complexity analysis
commonMistakes: Confusing DFS preorder with level order
Modifying queue while looping without fixing level size snapshot

transcript: Candidate: Level order traversal is naturally solved using Breadth-First Search with a queue. First, if root is null, return an empty array. We push root to the queue. While queue is not empty, we get the current level size: let levelSize = queue.length. We loop levelSize times, pop the front node, add its value to a currentLevel array, and enqueue its left and right children if they exist. After the inner loop, push currentLevel to result. The time complexity is O(N) because we visit each node once. Space complexity is O(N) because the queue stores nodes, at most N/2 at the bottom level of a balanced tree. Test case: a 3-node tree [1, 2, 3] gives [[1], [2, 3]].
notes: Good implementation of BFS with queue level snapshot. Correct complexity and null check. Testing is minimal.
